questions: Do you experience these jerks when you are not being examined?
Do the jerks stop if you close your eyes or look away while the hammer is brought toward your limb?
Does actually tapping the tendon trigger the same movement?
Can the jerks be triggered by watching another object move toward the limb?
Can the jerks be triggered by unexpected sounds or touch?
Do the jerks occur during voluntary movement of the affected limb?
Can you voluntarily suppress the jerks?
Do you feel an urge or build-up of tension before a jerk that is relieved afterward?
Do you remain fully aware during the jerks?
Have you ever lost awareness, fallen, bitten your tongue, or lost bladder control during an episode?
Do the jerks occur in more than one limb?
Do you have weakness, numbness, altered sensation, or problems with balance?
Have the jerks changed markedly in frequency or severity from one occasion to another?
Did they begin after an injury, illness, operation, or frightening or stressful event?
Do you take medicines or substances that can cause jerking movements?
Have you previously had epilepsy or another neurological illness?
Does anyone in your family have similar jerking movements?

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Functional (psychogenic) stimulus-induced myoclonus—a functional movement disorder with visually triggered, voluntary motor responses and no structural, epileptic, metabolic, or toxic cause identified.

Alternative 1: Organic stimulus-sensitive myoclonus not detected by current EEG/EMG testing

Alternative 2: Startle epilepsy

Alternative 3: Hereditary hyperekplexia (startle disease)
